PM-001.basis: Identical external order, capture, reference and event IDs remain store-scoped after HTTP server recreation. The test rejects the previous session, authenticates again, reads distinct orders and alerts, and rejects cross-store acknowledgement without mutation.

PM-005.basis: Explicit tests exercise deadline boundaries, duplicate and out-of-order events, restart, immutable policy and original capture association, late fulfillment history and delayed on-time correction.

independent_runs.scope: Final production source; before additional HTTP restart-isolation test.

browser_evidence.source_binding: All six production hashes match browser-accepted/server.json.
observed: Late fulfillment and delayed on-time correction retain distinct histories and reduce active count to zero.
Acknowledgement focus and subsequent polling preserve focus on the alert card.
Logout returns to the access form.
Replacement phone screenshots show legible full-width cards; metrics record 390x844, scale 1 and no horizontal overflow.

limitations: Local records, locally signed commerce fixtures and stubbed PayPal verification; no authentic provider execution established.
HTTP server recreation uses the same database within the test process; host reboot and crash durability are not established.
Single-operator multi-store isolation does not establish separate merchant-account authorization.
Browser proof does not establish all PM-007 states.
Other PM requirements retain outstanding conditions.
No original CC acceptance changes; frozen private count remains 47/60.
